pill.desc: white to off-white lyophilized powder in a single-dose vial

tell: A HER2-directed conjugate delivering DM1, a maytansine derivative, under a boxed warning for liver and heart toxicity.

clues.text: Its DM1 component is 93% bound to human plasma proteins in vitro, and the liver is the primary organ for eliminating it.
A recombinant protein made in Chinese hamster ovary cells, carrying an average of 3.5 DM1 molecules, supplied as a sterile, preservative-free lyophilized powder.
Approved under a BLA as single-dose vials of 100 mg or 160 mg, given as an infusion every 3 weeks.
Boxed warning for hepatotoxicity, cardiac toxicity and embryo-fetal toxicity; no contraindications. Fatigue and nausea are among the most common adverse reactions.
Biomarker-selected metastatic breast cancer after a prior antibody and a taxane, and adjuvant treatment of early breast cancer with residual invasive disease.
Targets HER2, and after internalization releases DM1, which binds tubulin and disrupts microtubule networks, arresting the cell cycle.
The generic name begins with T and has two words and twenty letters.
